name: Battle of the Bulge
note: This plan shows the operation, not a single field: the formations are armies, divisions and task forces, and the battle lasted from 16 December 1944 to 25 January 1945. The accounts give the sectors from north to south and the Meuse as the goal to the west, so north is drawn at the top and the Germans attack from the right. The exact positions of the places on the plan, and the routes between them, are drawn by judgement; the accounts do not give them. The Fifteenth Army, the British forces on the Meuse, the 82nd Airborne Division and the German special operations are not drawn. The plan ends with the relief of Bastogne on 26 December and the halt short of the Meuse; the fighting went on for another month. The 106th Division stands for the two regiments that surrendered; its remaining regiment is drawn inside the force at St. Vith.

phases.title: Three German armies face the Ardennes front
phases.text: The Sixth Panzer Army stood in the north, the Fifth Panzer Army in the middle and the Seventh Army in the south. The U.S. 99th and 2nd Divisions, the 106th Division and VIII Corps held the line opposite them.
phases.quote: The Seventh Army, under General Erich Brandenberger, was assigned to the southernmost sector, near the Luxembourgish city of Echternach

phases.title: The assault opens and Peiper's group leads the north
phases.text: The Germans opened with a 90-minute artillery barrage and attacked all along the front. Kampfgruppe Peiper, charged with the main effort, left the Sixth Panzer Army's line late.
phases.quote: the Germans began the assault with a massive, 90-minute artillery barrage using 1,600 artillery pieces

phases.title: Two regiments of the 106th Division are surrounded
phases.text: The Fifth Panzer Army surrounded two largely intact regiments of the 106th Division in a pincer movement and forced their surrender.
phases.quote: They succeeded in surrounding two largely intact regiments (422nd and 423rd) of the 106th Division in a pincer movement and forced their surrender

phases.title: The northern shoulder holds
phases.text: The 99th and 2nd Divisions repelled an advance by volksgrenadier and armoured units of the Sixth Panzer Army. This forced the German spearhead onto less favourable routes further south and slowed its advance.
phases.quote: forcing them to divert their offensive spearhead onto less favorable routes further south

phases.title: Peiper turns south and attacks Stavelot
phases.text: Peiper turned south to detour round Hünningen and arrived in front of Stavelot. He attacked it on 18 December, but the Americans evacuated a large fuel depot before he could take the town.
phases.quote: Kampfgruppe Peiper attacked Stavelot on 18 December but was unable to capture the town before the Americans evacuated a large fuel depot.

phases.title: The defenders fall back to Elsenborn Ridge
phases.text: The 12th SS Panzer Division renewed its advance into Krinkelt, and the defenders were ordered to break contact and abandon the twin villages. They reestablished their positions on Elsenborn Ridge.
phases.quote: the defenders were ordered to break contact, abandon the twin villages and reestablish positions on the strategic boomerang shaped Elsenborn Ridge.

phases.title: St. Vith slows the Fifth Panzer Army
phases.text: The defenders of St. Vith, led by the 7th Armored Division, resisted the German attacks and slowed the advance. The 2nd Panzer Division spearheaded the Fifth Panzer Army.
phases.quote: successfully resisted the German attacks, significantly slowing the German advance

phases.title: St. Vith is evacuated
phases.text: At Montgomery's orders the town of St. Vith was evacuated on 21 December. The American troops fell back to entrenched positions in the area, which presented an obstacle to the German advance.
phases.quote: At Montgomery's orders, St. Vith was evacuated on 21 December; U.S. troops fell back to entrenched positions in the area

phases.title: The defenders retreat west of the Salm
phases.text: By 23 December the Germans had shattered the flanks of the defenders and their position became untenable. The American troops were ordered to retreat west of the Salm River.
phases.quote: the defenders' position became untenable and U.S. troops were ordered to retreat west of the Salm River

phases.title: The 101st Airborne reaches Bastogne
phases.text: The struggle for the villages and strong points slowed the German attack enough for the 101st Airborne Division to reach Bastogne by truck on the morning of 19 December.
phases.quote: to reach Bastogne by truck on the morning of 19 December.

phases.title: Bastogne is cut off
phases.text: The panzer columns swung past on either side and cut Bastogne off on 20 December, but did not secure the crossroads. By 21 December the Germans had surrounded the town.
phases.quote: The panzer columns swung past on either side, cutting off Bastogne on 20 December

phases.title: The 2nd Panzer Division reaches Foy-Notre-Dame
phases.text: On 22 and 23 December German forces reached the woods of Foy-Notre-Dame, a few kilometres ahead of Dinant. On 24 December parts of the 2nd Panzer Division were in sight of the Meuse, the furthest German advance west.
phases.quote: On 22/23 December German forces reached the woods of Foy-Notre-Dame, only a few kilometers ahead of Dinant.

phases.title: The 2nd Armored Division attacks the spearheads
phases.text: The U.S. 2nd Armored Division attacked in an attempt to cut off the spearheads of the 2nd Panzer Division at the Meuse. As a result parts of the 2nd Panzer Division were cut off.
phases.quote: the 2nd Armored Division attempted to attack and cut off the spearheads of the 2nd Panzer Division at the Meuse

phases.title: The 4th Armored Division breaks through to Bastogne
phases.text: On 26 December the spearhead of the 4th Armored Division, supplemented by the 26th Infantry Division, broke through and opened a corridor to Bastogne. The siege had lasted barely a week.
phases.quote: the spearhead of Gen. Patton's 4th Armored Division, supplemented by the 26th (Yankee) Infantry Division, broke through
